title: Quick Pro GR:ONE – Review and Winter Test Ride

takeaways.text: The cut-out seatpost visibly flexes and makes the rear comfortable; the cockpit feels comparatively harsh with some rattle, and pairs awkwardly with SRAM's new levers until he added tape under the hoods.
His 44 mm Tufo Thunderos inflate to 46.5 mm, which he calls about the maximum the frame takes; at 25–28 psi he had not needed wider tires on his flat local gravel.
The stock post gave about 78 mm setback with the saddle slammed forward; the zero-offset AR:ONE post (supplied by his retailer) reduced it to about 60 mm and solved his fit issue.
His race-ready build with SRAM Force XPLR, Yoeleo NxT wheels and SPD pedals weighs 7.82 kg; he paid just under €5,500 in total.
After 300 km including a snowy 100 km group ride, a crit circuit and a local climb PR, he found it comfortable, confident and fast, with no toe overlap for his size-46 shoes on 165 mm cranks.

disclosure: The creator presents this as a review of his own build; any undisclosed commercial relationship remains unknown.
summary: Concise owner review and winter test ride of a GR:ONE build, useful for fit, comfort, and build context rather than specification proof.
